NS8 was a Las Vegas fraud-prevention software company that scored online transactions and flagged fake orders, bots and chargeback risk for e-commerce merchants, selling subscriptions to online retailers and payment-facing businesses. It was founded around 2012, and Crunchbase shows roughly $158 million raised, mostly in a 2020 round. In late 2020 US regulators alleged the company had overstated its revenue and customer numbers, and it was later placed into receivership. B2B only, with no consumer brand awareness, and that history makes it a poor sponsorship prospect.

Nutmeg is a London-based digital wealth manager, founded in 2011, offering managed investment portfolios, ISAs, pensions and junior accounts through an app and website, with fees charged as a percentage of assets under management. Customers are UK retail savers, with hundreds of thousands of accounts and several billion pounds of assets. JPMorgan Chase acquired it in 2021 and rebranded it as part of its UK digital bank offering, Chase. Nutmeg was one of the first UK robo-advisers and is reasonably well known among younger savers, but it is now a subsidiary of a global bank.

Pocket Gems is a San Francisco mobile games publisher founded in 2009 by former Google engineers. Its best-known titles are the free-to-play strategy game War Dragons and the interactive story app Episode, which offered serialised choose-your-story fiction to teenage and young adult audiences; it earns money from in-app purchases and advertising. Backed by Sequoia and others with about $155 million raised, it had hundreds of millions of downloads. Privately held. Consumer-facing apps with strong reach among mobile gamers, but low brand recognition outside the gaming community.

Privitar is a London data privacy software company founded in 2014 that helps large organisations de-identify, mask and govern sensitive data so it can be used for analytics and AI while meeting rules such as GDPR. Customers are banks, insurers, healthcare and telecom enterprises in the UK, US and Europe, paying software subscriptions. Crunchbase shows about $150 million raised, including a 2020 Series C. Informatica acquired Privitar in 2023. Purely B2B with little public brand awareness, so it has limited sponsorship appeal beyond enterprise hospitality.

Rebellion Defense is a Washington, D.C. company, founded around 2019, that builds artificial intelligence and software products for the US Department of Defense and allied governments, including tools for secure software delivery, mission planning and cyber defence. Customers are government and defence agencies, and revenue comes from software and services contracts. Crunchbase shows about $150 million raised in a 2021 round, which valued the company at around $1 billion. It was a venture-backed start-up founded by former Obama-era officials and defence technologists. Pure B2G, with almost no consumer visibility.

Revolution Foods is a US company founded in 2006 by Kirsten Tobey and Kristin Richmond that prepares and delivers healthier ready-to-eat meals, mainly to school districts, charter schools and other institutions, and later also sold meal kits and grocery products to families. Revenue comes from school meal programmes, partly government-funded, and from direct and retail sales. Crunchbase shows about $157 million raised from impact and growth investors. Headquartered in California. The brand is known in US education and nutrition circles but has little mainstream consumer recognition.

SI Group is a global specialty chemicals manufacturer headquartered in The Woodlands, Texas, with roots in Schenectady, New York. It makes antioxidants, resins, intermediates and other additives used in plastics, rubber, fuels, coatings, adhesives and tyres, selling to industrial manufacturers worldwide. It operates plants and sites across North America, Europe and Asia and has thousands of employees. It is privately held with private-equity backing. Crunchbase shows $150 million of financing in late 2025. B2B only, with little consumer awareness, and limited sponsorship relevance.

Snap Kitchen is an Austin, Texas company, founded around 2010, selling fresh, chef-prepared healthy meals such as low-carb, gluten-free and high-protein dishes. It sold through its own stores, in-store shelves and delivery or meal plans to health-conscious urban consumers in Texas and nearby states, earning money from per-meal retail sales and subscriptions. Crunchbase shows about $154 million raised. It was a regional consumer brand with dozens of stores at its peak and has since changed ownership and shrunk, so its current scale is unclear.

Stack Overflow is the question-and-answer site for programmers, founded in 2008 in New York by Jeff Atwood and Joel Spolsky. Tens of millions of developers use it monthly to find code answers; it earns money from employer advertising and recruiting, and from Stack Overflow for Teams, a paid knowledge-sharing product for companies. Prosus, the owner of Naspers' internet assets, bought it in 2021 for about $1.8 billion. Very well known among software engineers, but a B2B and developer brand rather than a mass-market consumer name.

TEMPOE is a Cincinnati-based lease-to-own financing company, founded in 2009, that lets consumers with limited credit lease items such as mattresses, furniture, tyres and electronics from retailers and pay in instalments, with the retailer paid up front. Revenue comes from lease payments and fees. Customers are US retailers and non-prime shoppers. Crunchbase shows about $150 million raised, mainly debt-style funding in 2017. A consumer finance business operating mostly behind retail partners, so it has little direct consumer brand awareness.

Terminus is a technology company based in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China, that Crunchbase describes as helping traditional businesses transform for the internet era, with information services among its listed industries. Funding shown is about CN 1.03 billion yuan, with the latest round in September 2021. The input does not give its products, customers or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

True Fit is a Boston-based data platform, founded in 2008, that helps fashion retailers and brands recommend the right size and style to each shopper using a database of garment and consumer fit data, reducing returns. Customers are apparel and footwear retailers and brands worldwide, who pay subscription and usage fees. Crunchbase shows about $157 million raised, with a late-2021 round. B2B technology that appears behind the scenes on retail websites, so consumers rarely know the brand name, though it processes data on hundreds of millions of shoppers.

Waves Platform is a blockchain company founded by Alexander Ivanov in 2016, after an initial coin offering, offering the WAVES token and a platform for launching custom tokens, decentralised exchange trading and smart contracts, with the Neutrino stablecoin among its projects. Users are crypto traders and developers, and the Waves ecosystem earns through token economics and transaction fees. Crunchbase lists a Moscow location and about $158 million of funding. Its profile was damaged by the 2022 stablecoin depeg, and it is known only within the crypto community.

X-FAB is a semiconductor foundry specialising in analogue and mixed-signal chips, silicon carbide and MEMS, producing wafers for other companies' designs, especially for automotive, industrial and medical customers. It operates fabs in Erfurt and Dresden in Germany, Itzehoe, Corbeil-Essonnes in France, Kuching in Malaysia and Lubbock in the USA, and has roughly 4,000 employees and revenue of several hundred million to about a billion euros. Listed on Euronext Paris under XFAB. Pure B2B with little consumer recognition, though it is a notable supplier to car makers.

Xiu.com is a Shenzhen-based Chinese online fashion marketplace that sold domestic and imported apparel, shoes, accessories and luxury goods to consumers, with brands and merchants listing on the platform and paying commissions. Crunchbase shows about $150 million raised, the latest round in 2015, and it positioned itself as a leading global fashion platform. It was an early player in cross-border fashion e-commerce but was overshadowed by larger platforms such as Tmall and JD.com, and its current activity is unclear.

Pegasus Airlines is a Turkish low-cost carrier based at Istanbul Sabiha Gokcen Airport and founded in 1990. It operates a young Airbus fleet of well over 100 aircraft on domestic, European, Middle Eastern and Central Asian routes and carries over 30 million passengers a year, making money from low fares plus ancillary sales such as baggage, seats and onboard retail. Listed on Borsa Istanbul as PGSUS, with Esas Holding the controlling shareholder. A well-known consumer brand in Turkey and neighbouring markets, with an active interest in sports sponsorship.

Turkiye Sigorta is Turkey's largest insurer, offering non-life insurance such as motor, property, health and accident cover, plus pension products through its group, sold via agents, brokers, banks and digital channels to individuals and businesses across Turkey. It is based in Istanbul and controlled by the Turkey Wealth Fund, a state sovereign fund, after the 2020 stock-market listing on Borsa Istanbul as TURSG. Premiums run to tens of billions of Turkish lira. A well-known consumer financial brand at home, with scope for sponsorship in the Turkish market.

Aktia Bank is a Finnish bank founded in 1825 as a savings bank, headquartered in Helsinki. It offers retail banking, mortgages, savings, wealth management, asset management and life insurance to private customers, SMEs and institutions, mainly in Finland, with a large part of its earnings coming from asset management. It has several hundred thousand customers and around 1,000 employees and manages more than 10 billion euros of assets. Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki as AKTIA. A well-known domestic finance brand in Finland with a sponsorship history in local sport and culture.

Asia Aviation Public Company is the Bangkok-based holding company that owns Thai AirAsia, the Thai low-cost carrier operating the AirAsia brand from Don Mueang airport. The airline flies domestic and regional routes with a fleet of Airbus A320-family jets and earns from low fares, baggage, seats and food sales. Passengers are mostly Thai and regional leisure travellers, with traffic running to many millions a year. Listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand as AAV, with AirAsia Group as a major shareholder. The AirAsia brand is very visible across Southeast Asia and active in sports sponsorship.

Bambuser is a Stockholm software company, founded in 2007, offering live video shopping: its platform lets brands and retailers run shoppable livestreams on their own websites and apps, and charges subscription and usage fees. Customers include fashion, beauty and consumer-electronics retailers across Europe, North America and Asia. It started as a mobile live-streaming app before moving to enterprise e-commerce. Listed on Nasdaq First North Growth Market in Stockholm as BUSER. B2B, with limited brand awareness among consumers, and a small company by revenue.

Banco Santander-Chile is the Chilean unit of Spain's Santander Group, based in Santiago and one of the country's largest banks by loans and customers. It offers retail, corporate and wealth banking, mortgages, cards, consumer credit and treasury services through hundreds of branches and digital channels, serving millions of customers. Santander Group holds a majority stake, and the bank is listed on the Santiago exchange and on the NYSE as BSAC. Santander is a high-profile sports sponsor globally, and the bank is a very visible consumer finance brand in Chile.

Clarivate is an information services company, headquartered in London and Philadelphia and incorporated in Jersey, that provides research and IP data to universities, governments and companies. Its brands include Web of Science, Journal Citation Reports, Derwent, CompuMark trademark services, Cortellis life-sciences data and, after 2021, ProQuest. It was spun out of Thomson Reuters in 2016 and listed on the NYSE as CLVT through a 2019 SPAC merger. Revenue is around 2.5 billion dollars, with roughly 11,000 staff. B2B, well known in academia but not to consumers.

Clearfield is a Minneapolis company that designs and makes fibre-optic connectivity products, including fibre management, enclosures, cabling and test equipment, used by broadband and telecommunications providers to deliver fibre to homes and businesses. Customers are mostly small and mid-size US telecom operators, rural carriers and cable companies, plus some international buyers. Listed on Nasdaq as CLFD, with revenue of a few hundred million dollars at its peak. Pure B2B with a small employee base and no consumer brand recognition, so it is an unlikely sponsor.

creditshelf is a Frankfurt financial technology company founded in 2014 that ran an online platform for lending to small and mid-sized German businesses, using algorithm-based credit assessment and matching companies with institutional lenders, then earning fees on arranged loans. It listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2019 under CSQ. It financed a relatively small loan volume and reported losses, and later restructured its business model. Crunchbase shows about 100 million euros raised. A small niche lender with little consumer recognition.

Global-e is a cross-border e-commerce platform, founded in 2013 and operating mainly out of Israel, that lets merchants sell to shoppers abroad by handling local pricing, duties and taxes, payments, shipping and returns. Customers are big fashion, beauty and lifestyle brands such as those on Shopify, with Shopify as a key partner and shareholder. It listed on Nasdaq as GLBE in 2021 after funding rounds, with Crunchbase showing about 100 million dollars from 2020. B2B and mostly invisible to shoppers, so low brand awareness.

Inpixon is a technology company, with a head office in Palo Alto, California and a German operation in Berlin, that sold indoor positioning and real-time location systems, sensors and analytics, tracking people and assets inside buildings such as offices, factories and hospitals. Customers are enterprises and government. It was listed on Nasdaq as INPX and later merged with XTI Aerospace in 2024 and was renamed. Crunchbase shows about 104 million dollars raised. B2B, with little consumer awareness.

Lucibel is a French industrial lighting company based in Barentin, Normandy, that designed and sold LED lighting, including connected lighting for retail, offices and industrial sites, and offered lighting-as-a-service and energy-efficiency work. Customers are businesses, retailers and public authorities in France and abroad. It was listed on Euronext Growth in Paris and had a small revenue base, reporting losses over the years. Crunchbase shows about 68.8 million euros raised. B2B with little brand awareness.

Malta International Airport operates Malta's only commercial airport at Luqa, handling passenger services, airport retail, parking, property rental and airline charges. Traffic runs to well over eight million passengers a year, mostly leisure travellers from the UK, Italy, Germany and elsewhere in Europe. It is listed on the Malta Stock Exchange as MIA, with Flughafen Wien and the Maltese government among its shareholders. Crunchbase shows a Valletta location and about 105 million euros of financing. A visible national infrastructure brand for tourists, but a minor consumer name abroad.

mCloud Technologies is a Vancouver-based software company selling AssetCare, an artificial intelligence and IoT platform for monitoring and optimising building systems, energy use and industrial assets. Customers include commercial real estate owners, healthcare campuses and industrial operators in North America and Europe, who pay software subscriptions and services fees. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange and on Nasdaq as MCLD. Crunchbase shows roughly 102 million dollars raised. B2B, small-cap, and little public awareness.

Minesto is a Swedish marine energy technology company based near Gothenburg that develops Dragon-class underwater kites, which fly in a figure-of-eight pattern in tidal and ocean currents to generate electricity from slow-moving water. It has run pilots in the Faroe Islands with the utility SEV and in Northern Ireland and Wales, supported by EU and national grants, and is pre-commercial with little revenue. Listed on Nasdaq First North in Stockholm as MINEST. B2B and very small, with no consumer brand, though its renewable positioning might suit a sustainability campaign.

MTN Uganda is the Ugandan subsidiary of South Africa's MTN Group and the country's leading mobile operator, based in Kampala. It provides voice, data, SMS and mobile money (MoMo) services to a very large share of the population, with well over ten million subscribers. It listed on the Uganda Securities Exchange in 2021 after a public offering, with MTN Group remaining the majority owner. A high-visibility consumer brand across the country, long active in sponsorship of football and music in Uganda.

Quanyuantang is a company in Chengdu, Sichuan, China, that Crunchbase tags under e-commerce and medical industries, and the input marks it as coming from a search of listed companies. The latest funding shown is about CN 580 million yuan in November 2020. The input does not describe its products, customers or business model beyond these tags. Samsung Card is a South Korean credit card company based in Seoul, issuing Samsung-branded credit and debit cards, and offering instalment, card loans and marketing and payment services to millions of cardholders, earning from merchant fees, interest and fees. It is one of Korea's biggest card issuers, with Samsung Life Insurance as the biggest shareholder and a listing on the Korea Exchange as 029780. It is part of the Samsung group, with strong awareness among Korean consumers, and sponsors some cultural and sports activity.

Semantix is a Sao Paulo data and artificial intelligence software company that offers a data platform, analytics and AI tools to Latin American enterprises, helping banks, retailers and telecoms organise and exploit data. Customers pay software and service fees. It listed on Nasdaq as STIX in 2022 through a merger with a special-purpose acquisition company, Alpha Capital. It is a small-to-mid-size company by revenue, with offices in Brazil and other Latin American countries. B2B, with little consumer brand awareness.

Shandong Longda Meat Foods is a Chinese poultry processor based in Yantai, Shandong, that raises, slaughters and processes chickens and sells chilled and frozen chicken and prepared meat products. It exports significant volumes, notably to Japan, and sells through domestic retailers and food service. It is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. Crunchbase shows about CN 950 million yuan of financing. It is a major regional agribusiness, mostly B2B, with little consumer recognition abroad.

Ted Baker is a London fashion brand founded in 1988 in Glasgow by Ray Kelvin, known for tailored menswear, womenswear, accessories and fragrances with a quirky British style, sold through its own shops, department stores and online in dozens of countries. It was listed on the London Stock Exchange until Authentic Brands Group bought it in 2022 for about 211 million pounds, and the retail business then ran into financial trouble, closing stores in the UK and the US. Retail operations now sit with licensing partners. A well-known premium fashion name.

UIGreen is an electronics and hardware company in Suzhou, Jiangsu, China, that Crunchbase tags under electronics and hardware, and the input shows it was found through a search for listed companies. Latest funding listed is about CN 690 million yuan in September 2022. The input does not describe specific products, customers or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Archosaur Games, operating as Zulong Entertainment, is a Beijing mobile game developer and publisher known for role-playing and card games based on Chinese licences, such as titles built on the Douluo Dalu novels. It earns revenue from in-game purchases across China and some overseas markets. It listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange as 9990 in 2020. Crunchbase shows about 64.6 million dollars raised. A consumer-facing games business with strong user reach in China, but little brand recognition elsewhere.

Borqs Technologies is a Santa Clara, California company with most of its operations in China and India, providing Android-based software and hardware for connected devices, including software for smartphones and Internet of Things products and later electric vehicle and tablet businesses. Customers are phone makers, telecom operators and enterprises. It listed on Nasdaq as BRQS in 2017 through a SPAC merger with Pacific Special Acquisition Corp, and has had accounting and governance problems. Crunchbase shows about 71 million dollars raised. B2B with little public awareness.

Brenmiller Energy is an Israeli company, based in Rosh Ha'ayin, that makes thermal energy storage systems called bGen, which heat crushed rock to store energy from solar, wind or the grid and release it later as steam or hot air for industry and district heating. Customers are industrial plants and utilities in Europe, Israel, the US and Asia, buying equipment and projects. Listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange and on Nasdaq as BNRG. A small company with small revenue and no consumer profile.

BurgerFi is a US fast-casual restaurant company, based in Florida, running the BurgerFi premium burger chain and, after a 2021 purchase, Anthony's Coal Fired Pizza & Wings, mostly through franchised and company-owned restaurants with a few hundred sites. Customers are US consumers dining in or ordering takeaway, and revenue comes from restaurant sales and franchise royalties. It listed on Nasdaq as BFI in 2020 through a SPAC merger with Opes Acquisition, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2024. A regional consumer brand with modest awareness and a weak financial position.

Dealicious is a company in Seoul, South Korea, that Crunchbase tags under B2B e-commerce, and the input shows it came from a search of listed companies. Funding shown is about 79 billion Korean won, with the latest round in January 2022. The input does not describe what it sells, who its customers are, or its ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Dobot is a Shenzhen robotics company, founded in 2015, that makes desktop and collaborative robot arms, the Nova and CR series, for factories, education, laboratories, retail and food service. It sells to manufacturers and system integrators in China and exports to many countries, earning from hardware, software and services. The company, backed by Chinese and international investors, listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in December 2024. It has a few hundred to a thousand employees. B2B, with little consumer awareness, though known in robotics and education circles.

Dodla Dairy is an Indian dairy company based in Hyderabad, founded in 1995 by the Dodla family, that collects milk from farmers and sells liquid milk, curd, ghee, butter, paneer and other products under the Dodla brand, mainly in southern India and with a presence in parts of Africa. Customers are households and retailers, with a large procurement network of farmers and large processing capacity. It listed on the NSE and BSE in 2021. A regional consumer food brand with strong recognition in south India and limited awareness elsewhere.

eDreams ODIGEO is a Barcelona online travel group, formed by merging eDreams, Go Voyages, Opodo and Travellink, which sells flights, hotels and packages to consumers in more than 30 countries through the eDreams, Opodo, Go Voyages and Travellink brands. Its main product is a subscription programme, eDreams Prime, with millions of paying members who pay an annual fee for discounted travel; it also earns commissions and advertising revenue. Owned partly by PE funds Permira, Ardian and others, and listed on the Spanish Stock Exchange as EDR. A recognised consumer travel brand in Europe.

Engine Media Holdings, which later became Engine Gaming and Media, is a Toronto-based group, with offices in New York, that owned esports, gaming and media assets, including the data and streaming business Stream Hatchet, the Eden Games racing mobile developer and the Frankly Media publishing platform, and earned revenue from advertising, analytics and games. It was listed on the TSX Venture Exchange and Nasdaq, formerly as Torque Esports. Crunchbase shows about 60.7 million dollars raised. A small-cap, mostly B2B and media business, with niche awareness among esports fans.

FIGS is a Santa Monica direct-to-consumer healthcare apparel brand, founded in 2013 by Heather Hasson and Trina Spear, selling medical scrubs, lab coats, underscrubs and everyday wear to nurses, doctors, dentists and vets, mainly online across the US and in other countries. It listed on the NYSE as FIGS in May 2021 and has annual revenue of around half a billion dollars, with millions of active customers. Well known among healthcare workers, with a social-media driven brand, and it has run ambassador and sponsorship programmes.

Finger is a company based in Yongdungpo, Seoul, South Korea, tagged on Crunchbase as asset management and finance, and the input shows it was found in a search of listed companies. Funding shown is about 87.5 billion Korean won, with the latest figure in August 2026. The input does not describe its products, customers or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Gridwiz is a Seoul energy technology company that supplies electric vehicle charging, demand response and energy management software and equipment, helping utilities and large energy users shift and balance electricity use through a virtual power plant approach. Customers are power companies, charging operators and commercial building owners in Korea, with some overseas pilots. It is listed in Korea. Funding shown is about 91 billion Korean won. B2B infrastructure, with low consumer awareness, though its charging and clean-energy theme can suit sustainability positioning.

JZ Capital Partners is a Guernsey-registered investment trust, managed from London and listed on the London Stock Exchange as JZCP, that invested in US and European private companies, mainly mezzanine and equity stakes alongside the sponsor Jordan/Zalaznick, and later in US residential real estate. It earns returns from investment income and realised gains, and has been returning capital to shareholders and winding down its portfolio. A small financial vehicle with no consumer brand, so very limited sponsorship relevance.

Luka Koper is the operator of the Port of Koper, Slovenia's only commercial seaport on the Adriatic, based in Koper. It handles containers, cars, bulk cargo, liquid cargo and general cargo, and provides logistics and rail connections to central Europe, with annual cargo volumes of around 20 million tonnes and about 1 million containers. The Slovenian state and its funds are main shareholders, and the shares are listed on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange. A B2B port business with little consumer recognition.

NextPoint Financial is a financial services company based in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, and the input shows it was found in a search of listed companies. Funding shown is about 74 million dollars, with the latest round in November 2022. The input gives no description of its products, customers or ownership beyond the financial services tag. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Novaturas is a Lithuanian tour operator based in Kaunas that sells package holidays and charter flights to leisure destinations such as Turkey, Egypt, Spain and Greece, mainly to consumers in Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, through its own offices and travel agencies. It has operated since 1999 and sends several hundred thousand travellers a year. The company is listed on Nasdaq Vilnius and the Warsaw Stock Exchange. A well-known holiday brand in the Baltics, but with a narrow regional market.

Pertamina Geothermal Energy is Indonesia's leading geothermal power company, a listed subsidiary of the state-owned oil and gas group Pertamina, based in Jakarta. It operates geothermal fields such as Kamojang, Lahendong, Ulubelu and Lumut Balai in Java, Sumatra and Sulawesi, selling steam and electricity mainly to the state utility PLN under long-term contracts. It listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange as PGEO in 2023 in one of the largest recent Indonesian IPOs. B2B with limited consumer visibility, but a clean-energy profile within the Pertamina group.

QuickFee is an Australian fintech, headquartered in Sydney, with its main business in the US, that provides payment plans and financing so clients of accounting and tax firms can pay professional fees in instalments, while the firm gets paid immediately. It earns from interest and fees on the financed amounts. It listed on the Australian Securities Exchange as QFE. Crunchbase shows about 72.8 million dollars raised. A niche B2B financial service with little consumer recognition.

Rivalry is a Toronto company, founded around 2016, that runs an online sportsbook and casino focused on esports and traditional sports betting, and a media arm covering gaming and betting content. Users are younger bettors in licensed markets such as Ontario and in other jurisdictions; revenue comes from betting margin and advertising. It is listed in Canada (TSXV: RVLY). Crunchbase shows about 66 million dollars raised. A niche gambling brand known among esports fans, and gambling advertising is heavily regulated.

Saint Marc is a Japanese cafe and bakery chain based in Okayama, operating Saint Marc Cafe, known for its chocolate croissants and light meals, with hundreds of locations across Japan and some in Asia. Its parent, Saint Marc Holdings, also runs other restaurant brands such as Cafe de Crie and Kyushu Jangara ramen, and sells through directly managed shops and franchises. It was listed in Tokyo and later went through a change of ownership. A familiar consumer brand in Japan with little recognition elsewhere.

Silan Microelectronics is a Hangzhou semiconductor maker, founded in 1997, that designs and manufactures integrated circuits, power devices, LED chips and modules, and runs its own fabs. Customers are manufacturers of home appliances, mobile devices, industrial equipment and electric vehicles, mainly in China. It is listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (600460) and has revenue in the billions of yuan. B2B, with low brand awareness among consumers, though a notable domestic chip supplier.

Stovekraft is a Bangalore company that makes and sells kitchen and home appliances in India, best known for the Pigeon brand of cookware, pressure cookers, gas stoves, induction cooktops and small appliances, plus Gilma and other brands. It sells through retail shops, e-commerce sites and its own stores to Indian households, with revenue of several billion rupees, and runs a large factory in Bangalore and Baddi. It listed on the Indian stock exchanges in 2021. A widely recognised household brand in India, often used in advertising and celebrity tie-ups.

StubHub is the ticket resale marketplace for concerts, sports and theatre, founded in 2000 in California and now based in New York. Fans buy and sell tickets on its websites and apps in dozens of countries, and it earns commissions from both buyers and sellers. eBay bought it in 2007 and sold it to Viagogo in 2020 for about 4 billion dollars; StubHub listed on the NYSE in 2025 under STUB. A very recognisable consumer brand with long-standing ties to sports leagues, venues and teams.

WonderFi is a Toronto company that built a regulated Canadian crypto trading group by acquiring platforms such as Bitbuy, Coinsquare, Blockchain.com's Canadian business and Tokens.com's holdings, offering trading, custody and decentralised finance access to retail and institutional users. It was listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange as WNDR. In 2025 Robinhood agreed to acquire the company. Crunchbase shows about 84 million dollars raised. Bitbuy and Coinsquare have some brand recognition among Canadian crypto traders.

Ashot Ashkelon is an Israeli aerospace manufacturer based in Ashkelon that makes landing gear, actuators and other precision mechanical components for military and civil aircraft, helicopters and other platforms. Its customers are Israeli and international aircraft makers, defence companies and air forces. It is part of the wider Israeli defence and aerospace supply chain. Crunchbase shows 120 million dollars of funding in January 2026. A B2B defence supplier with no consumer brand.

Barbeque Nation Hospitality is an Indian casual dining chain, based in Bangalore and founded in 2006, known for its live grill-on-the-table buffet, with around 200 restaurants across more than 100 Indian cities and a few outlets in the Gulf and Southeast Asia. It earns revenue from dine-in, delivery and packaged products. It listed on Indian stock exchanges in 2021. A well-known consumer dining brand in India, with solid awareness among urban families and groups.

Bigtincan is a sales enablement software company, founded in Sydney in 2011 and now headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, whose platform gives sales teams content, coaching and AI tools, widely sold to enterprise customers in finance, life sciences and technology. It grew by acquisitions including Zunos and Brainshark. It was listed on the Australian Securities Exchange as BTH and agreed to be taken over by Vector Capital in 2024. Crunchbase shows about 49 million dollars raised. B2B with no consumer awareness.

City Chic is a plus-size women's fashion company, headquartered in Sydney, Australia, that sells City Chic, Avenue and Evans branded clothing online and through shops in Australia, the US and the UK. It bought the US Avenue brand in 2020 out of bankruptcy, which explains the New Jersey address in the data. It is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange as CCX, with revenue of a few hundred million Australian dollars. A recognised niche fashion retailer in Australia, mainly marketed online.

Funding shown is about 59.2 billion Korean won, with the latest figure in June 2026. The input does not describe its titles, customers or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

DCM Shriram Industries is an Indian company, part of the DCM Shriram group and headquartered in New Delhi, with operations in sugar, industrial alcohol and ethanol, rayon tyre cord, fine chemicals and related products. Customers are industrial buyers, tyre manufacturers, fuel marketers and sugar consumers, mainly in India. It is listed on the Indian stock exchanges and operates factories in Uttar Pradesh and elsewhere. Crunchbase shows about 40 million dollars of financing. A B2B industrial business with little consumer visibility.

Eqva is a manufacturing company based in Valen, Hordaland, Norway, that Crunchbase tags under manufacturing and marine technology, and the input shows it came from a search of listed companies. Freshlocal Solutions is a Vancouver company that runs an online marketplace for local food, connecting farmers and independent food producers with consumers and businesses for delivery and pickup in British Columbia, and enabled groups to place orders in a farm-to-table model. It earns from sales commissions and software fees. It was listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. Crunchbase shows about 37.7 million dollars raised. A small regional start-up with limited awareness outside western Canada.

GomSpace is a Danish space technology company, based in Aalborg and founded in 2007, that designs and builds nanosatellites and CubeSats, along with subsystems, platforms and mission services for governments, space agencies and commercial customers, for example in Earth observation and communications. It has offices in Denmark, Sweden and Luxembourg and a staff of a few hundred. It is listed on Nasdaq First North in Stockholm as GOMX. B2B, small revenue, with little consumer recognition.

Groupe Flo is a French restaurant group, based in Courbevoie, that ran a collection of brasserie and restaurant brands including Brasserie Flo, Hippopotamus steakhouses, Taverne de Maitre Kanter and Bistro Romain, with franchised and owned restaurants across France. CapitalRise is a London property finance platform that arranges loans for property developers, mainly in prime London residential development, and lets investors lend into projects online, earning arrangement fees and interest margins. It was founded in the mid-2010s and is privately held, with Crunchbase indicating a financing of roughly 321 million pounds in 2024, likely a debt facility. A niche B2B financial firm with limited public awareness.

Community Healthcare Trust is a Franklin, Tennessee real estate investment trust that owns medical office buildings, outpatient and specialty hospitals, behavioural facilities and other healthcare properties in the United States, mainly in smaller markets, leasing them to physician groups, hospital operators and healthcare providers. It was founded in 2014 and is listed on the NYSE as CHCT. A B2B landlord with no consumer brand, though it is known among small-cap REIT investors.

Emtek Group, formally Elang Mahkota Teknologi, is a Jakarta-based Indonesian conglomerate with media, technology and healthcare businesses, including the free-to-air TV networks SCTV and Indosiar, the streaming service Vidio, and a large investment in the e-commerce firm Bukalapak, as well as the Mitra Keluarga hospital chain. It is listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange as EMTK, with controlling shareholders from the Sariaatmadja family. SCTV and Indosiar are household names in Indonesia, and the group broadcasts major sport, so it is a media partner more than a sponsor.

Fantawild is a Shenzhen-based Chinese culture and tourism company that designs, builds and operates theme parks, such as the Fantawild Adventure and Oriental Heritage parks, and makes animated content, including the Boonie Bears franchise of TV series and films. Revenue comes from park tickets, licensing, merchandise and technology and construction services for other parks. It operates dozens of parks in China and has some overseas projects. A recognised consumer entertainment brand in China, especially among families with children.

FDJ is the French national lottery and gaming group, short for Francaise des Jeux, based in Boulogne-Billancourt, operating Loto, Euromillions, scratch games and the Parions Sport betting brand across around 30,000 points of sale and online. It was privatised and listed on Euronext Paris in 2019, with the French state still a significant shareholder, and has since expanded into online betting by buying Kindred in 2024. Revenue is in the billions of euros. Highly recognised in France, and a long-running sports sponsor, including the Groupama-FDJ cycling team.

Finisar was a Sunnyvale, California maker of optical communications components, such as transceivers, wavelength-selective switches and 3D sensing lasers, sold to telecom equipment makers, data-centre operators and consumer electronics companies including Apple. It was listed on Nasdaq as FNSR and had revenue of over a billion dollars. II-VI acquired it in 2019 for about 3.2 billion dollars, and the combined business is now called Coherent. Crunchbase shows 390 million dollars of funding in 2017. A B2B component supplier that no longer exists as an independent company.

Gropyus is an Austrian construction technology start-up, based near Vienna and founded in 2020, that designs and builds sustainable, prefabricated timber-hybrid apartment buildings and smart homes using digital design and factory-built modules. Its customers are developers, municipalities and investors. It raised a large funding round in early 2026 according to Crunchbase, with about 370 million euros shown. A small, young company with a sustainability angle but low consumer brand awareness.

Maven Clinic is a New York digital health company, founded in 2014, offering virtual care for women's and family health, including fertility, pregnancy, postpartum, pediatrics, menopause and parenting support. Employers and health plans pay for the service as a benefit for their staff, who can access coaches and clinicians by video and chat. It serves millions of members in over a dozen countries and was valued at about 1.7 billion dollars in 2021. Backed by Oak HC/FT, General Catalyst, Sequoia and others. A B2B2C brand known among HR leaders and benefit users.

ProsperCap is a real estate firm in Singapore that describes itself as a multinational real estate investment and development group. Funding shown is about 310 million, with the latest figure in September 2024, in a currency not clearly given in the input. It lacks further details on its portfolio, markets, size or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

The South African National Roads Agency (SANRAL) is the state-owned agency, based in Pretoria, responsible for building, upgrading and maintaining South Africa's national road network of around 22,000 kilometres, including toll roads and the Gauteng freeway improvement project and its e-toll system. It is owned by the government and raises money from bonds and government funding as well as toll revenue. It has a high public profile in South Africa, but as a state road agency it has no consumer product and little commercial sponsorship activity.

Superstrada Pedemontana Veneta is the project company behind the Pedemontana Veneta toll motorway in northern Italy, a major road in the Veneto region between Vicenza and Treviso, based near Bassano del Grappa (the data wrongly lists Venezuela). It is a public-private concession involving the Veneto region and a construction consortium, financed with debt and toll income, with a total cost of several billion euros. Funding shown is about 350 million euros. A B2B infrastructure concession, with local recognition only.

UDR is a Denver-area real estate investment trust, based in Highlands Ranch, Colorado, that owns, operates and develops apartment communities, with tens of thousands of homes in markets such as Boston, New York, the mid-Atlantic, Florida, Texas, California and Seattle. It earns rent from residents and is listed on the NYSE as UDR. Total assets run to over 10 billion dollars. A B2B landlord with consumer-facing apartment brands but no strong mainstream brand profile.

WEKA is a Campbell, California data platform company, previously WekaIO and founded in 2013, whose software provides a fast parallel file system for AI, machine learning, genomics, financial modelling and high-performance computing workloads, running on-premises and in the public cloud. Customers include AI labs, life-sciences firms, financial companies and cloud providers. It was valued at about 1.6 billion dollars in a 2024 round, with Crunchbase showing 415 million dollars raised. A B2B infrastructure company, with little consumer awareness.

Arrive Logistics is an Austin, Texas freight brokerage, founded in 2010, that arranges truckload transport for shippers and carriers across the US and Canada, using technology to match loads and price shipments. Customers are manufacturers, retailers and distributors, and revenue comes from the gap between what shippers pay and carriers are paid, in the billions of dollars a year. It has several thousand employees and has grown quickly. B2B, with little consumer awareness.

Atkore is a Harvey, Illinois manufacturer of electrical raceway products, such as conduit, cable, armoured cable and fittings, and of mechanical products such as strut and framing, used in construction, utilities and data centres. It sells through distributors to electrical contractors across the United States and in other markets, with revenue of over three billion dollars at its peak. It is listed on the NYSE as ATKR, having been separated from Tyco in 2011. B2B and industrial, with no consumer brand profile.

Billd is an Austin, Texas fintech company that provides financing for construction materials, letting contractors buy supplies on extended payment terms while suppliers get paid up front, using a digital application and credit assessment designed for the construction sector. It earns fees and interest. It was founded around 2018 and Crunchbase shows about 359 million dollars of funding, mostly in debt facilities. A niche B2B lender with low public awareness.

Fal is a San Francisco generative media platform, known as fal.ai, founded in 2021, that gives developers and companies a fast cloud inference API and infrastructure for running image, video, audio and 3D AI models, with customers building creative and consumer apps. It earns usage-based fees. It raised several large venture rounds in 2025 at valuations in the multiple billions, with Crunchbase showing about 338 million dollars raised. A developer-focused B2B brand, with little awareness among the general public.

FangDD is a Shenzhen online real estate platform, founded in 2011, that connects property agents, developers and buyers in China, offering listings, transaction services and data tools for agents and new-home sales. It is listed on Nasdaq, under the ticker DUO, since its 2018 IPO, and has faced losses and falling revenue as the Chinese property market weakened. Crunchbase shows about 366 million dollars raised. A B2B-oriented portal that had some brand reach among Chinese agents and homebuyers, but declining relevance.

Fibra Shop is a Mexican real estate investment trust, formally Fibra Shop Portafolios Inmobiliarios, which owns shopping centres and retail properties in Mexico and leases space to retail, food and service tenants, listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange as FSHOP. Revenue comes from rents. Crunchbase shows a financing of about 6.6 billion Mexican pesos in 2025. A property investment vehicle whose centres are known locally, but with little brand profile beyond investors.

First Bank of Nigeria, or FirstBank, is one of Nigeria's oldest and largest banks, founded in 1894 and based in Lagos, offering retail, commercial and corporate banking, cards, mobile and agency banking to millions of customers, with a branch network across the country and subsidiaries in the UK, France and several African countries. It is the main operating unit of FBN Holdings and is among Nigeria's best-known financial brands. FirstBank has a history of sponsorship in football and other national events in Nigeria.

Hupu is a Shanghai-based Chinese sports media and community company, whose Hupu app and website have a huge forum of sports fans, especially basketball and football, with news, live game discussion, e-commerce for sports products and events. It earns advertising, e-commerce and event revenue, and was founded in 2004. Venture investors back it, with Crunchbase showing about 338 million dollars raised. Strongly known with young Chinese male sports fans, so potentially a media or activation partner more than a sponsor.

Iluvatar CoreX is a Shanghai-based Chinese developer of general-purpose graphics processing units (GPUs) for AI training and inference and high-performance computing, selling chips, accelerator cards and software to data-centre and AI customers in China. It was founded in 2015 and is part of the domestic push to replace imported AI chips. Crunchbase shows about 353 million dollars raised. A B2B semiconductor business with little awareness outside the Chinese chip and AI industry.

isolved is a Charlotte, North Carolina human capital management software company that provides payroll, HR, benefits, time and attendance and talent software to small and mid-sized employers, sold through its own team and partner service firms. It serves tens of thousands of client businesses and several million employees in the US. It is privately held, with Crunchbase showing a 350 million dollar financing in 2025. B2B SaaS with strong visibility among HR buyers, but low consumer awareness.

Kaer is a Singapore-based provider of cooling-as-a-service, which designs, installs, owns and maintains cooling systems for buildings, data centres and industrial customers, who pay for the cooling they use instead of buying equipment. It operates in Singapore and other Asian markets, and has been backed by private investors. Crunchbase shows about 350 million dollars of financing in 2025, probably including debt facilities. A B2B energy-services company with a sustainability angle and no consumer brand profile.

LendUp was an Oakland, California online lender that offered short-term loans and credit-building products to people with poor credit, with a tiered programme that promised lower rates for responsible borrowers, and later a prepaid card. It was founded in 2012 and venture-backed, including by Google Ventures. The US consumer finance regulator fined it in 2016 and again later for misleading practices, and the business wound down in the early 2020s. Crunchbase shows about 361 million dollars raised. Not an attractive sponsorship partner.

Meati is a Boulder, Colorado food company that makes meat alternatives from mycelium, the root structure of fungi, selling products such as chicken-style cutlets and steak-style cuts in US grocery stores and restaurants. It was founded in 2019 and raised about 374 million dollars from investors including Bezos Expeditions and Siddhi Capital. It struggled financially from 2024, leading to a distressed sale. A consumer food brand with a modest retail presence, so its sponsorship potential is limited.

Modular is a Palo Alto AI infrastructure company, founded in 2022 by Chris Lattner, the creator of LLVM and Swift, and Tim Davis, that builds the Mojo programming language and the MAX platform for running AI models across different hardware. It sells to developers, AI companies and cloud providers, earning from software and enterprise licences. Backed by General Catalyst, GV and others, Crunchbase shows about 380 million dollars raised, with a valuation of 1.6 billion dollars. A developer-focused B2B brand with a following in the AI engineering community.

Physics Wallah is an Indian education technology company, based in Noida and founded by teacher Alakh Pandey, offering low-cost live and recorded classes, test series and books for school students and for entrance exams such as JEE and NEET, along with offline coaching centres. It has tens of millions of app users and hundreds of centres. Backed by WestBridge Capital and GSV Ventures, it listed on the Indian stock exchanges in late 2025. A highly recognised consumer education brand among Indian students and parents.

Rightmove is the UK's largest online property portal, based in Milton Keynes, where estate and letting agents and developers pay monthly fees to advertise homes to millions of visitors. It earns most of its revenue from agent subscriptions and has expanded into mortgages and rental referencing. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange in the FTSE 100 as RMV, with revenue of around 400 million pounds and high profit margins. A very well-known UK consumer brand.

Sawnee EMC is a Georgia electric membership cooperative based in Cumming, north of Atlanta, owned by its members, which distributes electricity to homes and businesses in Forsyth, Fulton, Dawson, Cherokee and nearby counties, and offers solar and energy efficiency services. It buys much of its power from the wholesale generation cooperative Oglethorpe Power. Revenue is in the hundreds of millions of dollars. Crunchbase shows about 369 million dollars of financing in 2024. A local utility with community presence, but no wider consumer brand.

Sennder is a Berlin digital freight forwarding company, founded in 2015, that runs a platform and network of carriers to move full truckloads across Europe and, after buying Uber Freight's European business in 2022, a larger share of European road freight. Customers are manufacturers, retailers and other shippers, and it earns on freight services and software. It has been funded by Lakestar, Scania and Bain Capital Ventures, among others, with Crunchbase showing about 340 million dollars raised. B2B, with little consumer awareness.

Shanghai Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone Development, usually called Waigaoqiao, is a Shanghai-listed company (SSE 600648) that develops and operates the Waigaoqiao free trade zone in Pudong, one of China's oldest, providing warehousing, bonded logistics, trading, property leasing and related services to importers and exporters. It is controlled by Shanghai state-owned interests, and funding shown is about 2.5 billion yuan. B2B, with low public awareness beyond Shanghai's logistics and trade circles.

Taaleem is a Dubai-based education company that owns and operates private schools and nurseries in the UAE, using British, American and international curricula, with around a dozen schools and tens of thousands of students, and also builds and manages schools for others. It earns tuition and management fees. It listed on the Dubai Financial Market in 2022 under TAALEEM. Crunchbase shows about 337 million dollars of financing. Well known to expatriate families in the UAE, though not a mass consumer brand.

Vastai Technologies is a Shanghai-based Chinese developer of AI inference chips and accelerator cards, serving data-centre, video and computing customers in China, as part of the country's drive for domestic AI semiconductors. It was founded in the late 2010s, and Crunchbase shows about 378 million dollars raised from investors. It sells to cloud providers, internet firms and server makers. A B2B chip business, with little awareness outside the AI chip industry.

Via Celere is a Madrid residential developer, one of Spain's largest, that builds and sells homes, mainly new apartments and houses, and also manages rental housing, across Spanish cities and regions. It was formed from Spanish real estate assets that investors such as Cerberus and then Varde Partners acquired from banks. Crunchbase shows about 320 million euros of financing in 2025. Customers are homebuyers and institutional investors. Its projects carry local names, so the Via Celere brand has moderate awareness within Spain.

Vorboss is a London-based provider of dedicated, ultra-fast full-fibre connectivity to businesses and data centres, building its own network under central London and expanding into other UK cities, and selling leased lines, internet access and wavelength services to firms in sectors such as finance, media and technology. It was founded in 2017 and has raised equity and debt, with Crunchbase showing about 250 million pounds. A B2B telecom brand with little public awareness, though it has run marketing in London.

Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis is the medical school of Washington University, with research and teaching tied to Barnes-Jewish Hospital and St. Louis Children's Hospital, a major recipient of US National Institutes of Health research funding and consistently ranked among the top US medical schools. It runs a large clinical and research enterprise with thousands of faculty, staff and students. A nonprofit academic institution, with a strong reputation in medicine but not a commercial consumer brand, so sponsorship fit is limited.

WeddingWire is a wedding planning marketplace and directory, founded in 2007 and based in Chevy Chase, Maryland, where engaged couples search for vendors such as photographers, venues and caterers, read reviews, build planning checklists and create websites, while vendors pay for advertising and lead generation. It operated in the US, Canada and several international markets. In 2018 it merged with The Knot to form XO Group-owned The Knot Worldwide. Crunchbase shows about 381 million dollars raised before the merger. A well-known wedding brand with strong consumer awareness.

ZJS Express, also known as Zhaijisong, is a Beijing-based Chinese logistics company that provides express parcel delivery, freight and supply chain services, with a long-established national network, serving businesses and consumers across China. It was founded in the 1990s as one of the early private express carriers. Funding shown is about 2.2 billion yuan, with the latest figure in April 2021. It is a recognised name in Chinese logistics, though smaller than SF Express and similar rivals.

Ajlan Sons for Commercial and Real Estate, whose full name refers to Abdulaziz Alajlan Sons for Trading and Real Estate, is a company based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in trading and property. Funding shown is about 300 million dollars, with the latest figure in August 2025. The input gives no industry tags, and does not detail its projects, brands or ownership; it is likely a family-owned Saudi business. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Beitel Group is a Brooklyn, New York single-family office that buys, develops and manages multifamily and mixed-use residential and commercial real estate, mainly in the New York area and other US markets. It invests the founder family's capital rather than raising it from the public. Crunchbase shows about 305 million dollars of financing in 2025. A private investor and landlord with little brand visibility beyond the New York property trade.

Bungalow Projects Bain Capital Real Estate JV is described in the input as a joint venture focused on real estate, with Bain Capital Real Estate as the backer, based in New York. Crunchbase shows about 304 million dollars of funding in October 2025. The input does not say what Bungalow Projects builds or operates, in which markets, or the size of its portfolio. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

CEC Bank is a Romanian state-owned bank, founded in 1864 as a savings bank and based in Bucharest, with one of the country's largest branch networks, serving individuals, small businesses and public bodies with savings, loans, cards and payments. It has millions of customers and a strong presence in smaller towns and rural areas. The Romanian state, through the Ministry of Finance, owns it, and Crunchbase shows about 300 million euros of funding. A long-established domestic consumer bank with strong awareness in Romania.

Celeste is a French internet and telecom operator, based in Champs-sur-Marne near Paris and founded in 1994, that supplies dedicated internet access, fibre connectivity, cloud and managed services to businesses, local authorities and operators, and owns its own network and data centres. It is a B2B telecom company with strong name recognition within French IT departments, and little among consumers. Funding shown is about 260 million euros, with the latest figure in June 2021.

Clutter is a Culver City, California on-demand storage and moving company, founded in 2013, that picks up household items, stores them in warehouses and returns them on request, and also provides moving services, charging monthly storage fees. It operated in dozens of US metropolitan areas and was funded by venture investors including Sequoia Capital and Atomico, with Crunchbase showing about 296 million dollars raised. A consumer service brand with modest, local awareness in the cities where it operates.

Couchbase is a software company, founded in 2008 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, listed here with a San Jose address, that sells a NoSQL cloud database platform, including Couchbase Capella, for building web, mobile and AI applications. Customers include large banks, airlines and retailers, and revenue is from subscriptions of around 200 million dollars a year. It listed on Nasdaq as BASE in 2021 and agreed to be taken private by Haveli Investments in 2025. A B2B developer brand with little consumer awareness.

DataDirect Networks, usually called DDN, is a US data storage company, founded in 1998 and based in the Los Angeles area (Chatsworth, now Santa Clara), selling high-performance storage systems and the EXAScaler and Infinia platforms for AI, supercomputing and analytics. Customers include research centres, AI labs, financial firms and cloud providers, and Nvidia is a close technology partner. Blackstone made a major investment in 2025. A B2B infrastructure brand well known in high-performance computing and with little consumer recognition.

Delgaz Grid is the Romanian natural gas and electricity distribution operator, based in Targu Mures and part of the E.ON group's Romanian business, which runs gas networks across central and northern Romania and delivers energy to households and businesses on behalf of suppliers. It is a regulated network business and earns fees set by the regulator. Funding shown is about 299 million dollars in late 2024. A utility with little consumer brand recognition separate from the E.ON name.

Earnest is a San Francisco lender, founded in 2013, offering student loan refinancing and private student loans, using data on the borrower's financial profile rather than just credit scores, to give lower rates to graduates in professional careers. Navient acquired it in 2017 for about 155 million dollars. It operates in the US, funds itself through loan sales and securitisation, and Crunchbase shows about 316 million dollars raised. A familiar fintech brand to US borrowers and graduates, but a subsidiary of a larger student-loan servicer.

EastGroup Properties is a real estate investment trust headquartered in Ridgeland, Mississippi, listed here as Jackson, that owns, develops and operates industrial distribution buildings in Sunbelt markets such as Texas, Florida, Arizona, California and the Carolinas, leased to a wide range of companies. It is listed on the NYSE as EGP and has a portfolio of over 400 buildings. Total assets are in the billions of dollars. A B2B landlord with a low profile outside the investor community.

Furlenco is an Indian furniture and appliance rental subscription company, based in Bengaluru and founded in 2012, that rents beds, sofas, wardrobes, appliances and electronics to urban households for monthly fees, with delivery and maintenance included, and also sells refurbished items. Customers are young professionals and families in about a dozen Indian cities. Backed by venture investors, with Crunchbase showing about 286 million dollars raised. A recognised consumer brand in Indian metros that has used active digital advertising.

Garofalo Health Care is an Italian private healthcare group, based in Rome, that owns and runs hospitals, outpatient clinics, diagnostic centres, rehabilitation and long-term care facilities, mostly in northern and central Italy, under local brands, working with public health service and private insurers. It was founded by the Garofalo family and listed on Borsa Italiana (Euronext Milan) as GHC in 2018. Crunchbase shows about 275 million euros of financing. A regional healthcare group with local brands and little national consumer branding.

Georgia Global Utilities (GGU) is a Georgian utility holding company, based in Tbilisi, that owns the water supply and sewerage business of Tbilisi and other regions, as well as hydropower plants and other renewable energy and waste assets. It is controlled by Georgia Capital, a company listed in London. The utility serves around a million people and businesses, with revenue from regulated water tariffs and electricity sales. Funding shown is about 300 million dollars, from 2024. Mostly a regulated infrastructure business with limited sponsorship interest.

Gilt Groupe was a New York online flash-sale retailer, founded in 2007, which sold designer fashion and home goods at discounted prices through members-only time-limited events. It was valued at over a billion dollars at its peak, and was bought by Hudson's Bay Company in 2016 for about 250 million dollars, then sold on to Rue La La in 2018. Crunchbase shows about 286 million dollars raised before the sale. A consumer shopping brand that was well known in the early 2010s and has reduced visibility today.

Halyk Bank is Kazakhstan's largest bank by assets, based in Almaty, offering retail, SME and corporate banking, insurance, brokerage, and the Halyk app and Halyk Market online marketplace. It has millions of customers in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan, with a large branch network, and is listed on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange and London as HSBK. A very recognisable consumer bank in Kazakhstan, with a strong sponsorship history there.

Hootsuite is a Vancouver software company, founded in 2008 by Ryan Holmes, whose platform lets businesses schedule posts, monitor, respond to and analyse activity across social networks such as Instagram, LinkedIn, X and Facebook. It earns subscription fees from small businesses, large corporations and agencies, with millions of users and customers in over 100 countries. Crunchbase shows about 300 million dollars raised, and it has bought companies including Uberflip and Talkwalker. A B2B brand known across the marketing world, symbolised by its owl logo.

Krutrim is an Indian artificial intelligence company based in Bengaluru, founded in 2023 by Bhavish Aggarwal, who also founded Ola, building large language models for Indian languages, cloud services, an AI assistant and custom AI chips. It became India's first AI unicorn in early 2024 after a funding round. Customers include developers and companies, plus consumers who use the Krutrim app, and Crunchbase shows about 304 million dollars raised. A visible Indian tech brand tied to Ola's founder.

Leap is an Indian study-abroad platform, formerly Leap Scholar, based in Bengaluru, that helps students apply to universities abroad, take English tests, get student loans and arrange visas and accommodation, earning fees from universities, lenders and students. It has counsellors and partnerships across countries such as the US, UK, Canada and Australia. Crunchbase shows about 318 million dollars of funding, with the latest round in early 2025. A consumer education brand with decent awareness among Indian students who plan to study abroad.

Meridia Capodagli is described in the input as a real estate company offering construction and property management services, with a location in Linden, New Jersey. Crunchbase shows about 286 million dollars of funding in October 2025. The input does not give its projects, size or ownership, and the funding may relate to a single development vehicle rather than a corporate round. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Minted is a San Francisco online marketplace and design company, founded in 2007, that sells wedding invitations, holiday cards, stationery, art prints and home decor, designed by an international community of independent artists chosen through design challenges. Customers are consumers in the US who buy cards and decor online, and artists receive royalties. Crunchbase shows about 297 million dollars raised from venture investors. A recognised consumer brand among affluent households that buy stationery online, though not a mass-market name.

Motiv Electric Trucks is a Foster City, California maker of electric powertrains and chassis for medium-duty commercial vehicles such as school buses, delivery trucks, shuttles and utility trucks, and it builds the EPIC chassis and the Argo electric truck. Customers are fleet operators, school districts and truck builders across the US, and it earns from vehicle and chassis sales. It was founded in 2009, and Crunchbase shows about 311 million dollars raised. A B2B fleet brand with a modest public profile.

Mythic is an Austin, Texas semiconductor company, founded in 2012 as a spin-out from the University of Michigan, that designs analogue compute-in-memory processors for running AI models at low power and low cost, particularly at the edge, and sells chips and development tools to makers of cameras, drones, industrial and automotive devices. It raised a large new round in 2025 after a restructuring, with Crunchbase showing about 293 million dollars raised. B2B hardware with a low profile outside the AI chip industry.

Petrovietnam Power Services, known as PV Power Services, is a Vietnamese company in Hanoi that provides operation, maintenance, repair and engineering services for power plants, including gas-fired and other thermal plants owned by PV Power and the PetroVietnam group. It is part of the state-owned oil and gas group's electricity segment. Funding shown is about 300 million dollars, with the latest figure in April 2024. A B2B services company with little public brand awareness.

Qingwei Intelligent Technology, also called Tsingmicro, is a Beijing company spun out of Tsinghua University that develops reconfigurable AI chips for training and inference and edge devices, and sells to server, camera and automotive makers in China. It is part of China's domestic AI chip sector. Funding shown is about 2.2 billion yuan, with the latest round in late 2025. A B2B semiconductor firm, with little brand recognition among general consumers.

Tachyum is a Las Vegas semiconductor company, with development staff in Slovakia, developing the Prodigy universal processor, a chip designed to combine CPU, GPU and AI functions for data centres, AI and high-performance computing. Customers would be hyperscale data-centre operators and supercomputing projects, and it has announced a deal for a large AI system in Europe, but volume product shipment has been repeatedly delayed. Crunchbase shows about 290 million dollars raised. A B2B chip start-up with little consumer awareness.

Target Healthcare REIT is a London-listed real estate investment trust, trading on the London Stock Exchange as THRL, that owns modern, purpose-built care homes in the UK, leased to care home operators on long inflation-linked leases. It has a portfolio of more than 90 homes worth around 700 million pounds, with a focus on sustainability. Revenue is from rents, and it is externally managed by Target Advisers. A B2B property investment company with no consumer brand awareness.

Tegethoff Development is a real estate development company based in St. Louis, Missouri, United States, whose Crunchbase industries include construction and interior design, and whose own description calls it a real estate development company. Funding shown is about 285 million dollars, with the latest figure in November 2025, which may relate to project financing. The input does not give its projects, size or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Texas Eastern Transmission is a Houston-based natural gas pipeline company that operates a large interstate pipeline system, stretching from Texas and the Gulf Coast to the US Northeast, carrying gas to utilities, power generators and industrial users. It is a subsidiary of Enbridge, having been part of Spectra Energy before Enbridge acquired it in 2017. Revenue comes from regulated transportation fees. The 300 million dollars shown relates to a debt issue. A B2B energy infrastructure unit with no consumer profile.

TVS Supply Chain Solutions is a global logistics and supply chain company, part of India's TVS group, with its headquarters in Chennai and a UK base in Slough, providing integrated services to automotive, technology, consumer and industrial customers, through inbound logistics, warehousing, freight and aftermarket services. It listed on the Indian stock exchanges in 2023 and operates in over 20 countries. Crunchbase shows about 317 million dollars raised. A B2B logistics brand, supported by the well-known TVS group name in India.

UBA Kenya is the Kenyan subsidiary of the United Bank for Africa Group, one of Nigeria's biggest banks, based in Nairobi, providing retail, SME and corporate banking, trade finance and payments to customers in Kenya, with a particular focus on Nigerian and pan-African trade. It is a small bank within the Kenyan market, with Crunchbase showing about 37.5 billion Kenyan shillings of funding in 2024. UBA is a major brand across Africa and has some experience of sports sponsorship, though the Kenyan arm is modest in profile.

Ulster University is a public university in Northern Ireland with campuses in Belfast, Coleraine, Derry/Londonderry and Jordanstown, with tens of thousands of students and a long record of research in subjects such as health sciences, engineering and creative technologies. It earns income from government funding, tuition fees and research grants. It is one of the largest universities on the island of Ireland. A non-commercial educational institution with strong local recognition and limited fit as a commercial sponsorship prospect.

Vedantu is a Bengaluru online tutoring and education technology company, founded in 2014, that provides live online classes, test preparation and one-to-one tutoring for school students in India and abroad, as well as offline centres. Revenue comes from course fees paid by parents. It has been backed by investors such as Tiger Global and Westbridge, with Crunchbase showing about 306 million dollars raised, and had layoffs and cost cuts after 2022. A well-known consumer education brand in India, with prior heavy advertising.

WeWork India is the Indian flexible office space operator, based in Bengaluru, with dozens of centres in cities such as Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi, Pune and Hyderabad. It is controlled by real estate developer Embassy Group, which bought the main stake from the global WeWork brand licence holder, and WeWork India lists its shares in India.
