Medium is a San Francisco online publishing platform, launched in 2012 by Twitter co-founder Evan Williams, where writers and readers publish and read essays and articles, supported by a paid membership programme that shares revenue with authors, along with publications on topics like technology and culture. It has tens of millions of monthly visitors. Crunchbase shows about 163 million dollars raised from venture investors. A consumer publishing brand with strong recognition among writers and tech readers.

NewLake Capital Partners is a Connecticut real estate investment trust, based in New Canaan, that owns industrial, cultivation and retail properties leased to licensed cannabis operators in the US, as a sale-leaseback landlord. It is internally managed and trades on the OTCQX market as NLCP. Funding shown is about 176 million dollars, from August 2022. A niche B2B landlord serving the cannabis sector, with no consumer brand, and sponsorship is constrained by the sector.

Nobia is a Swedish kitchen company, based in Stockholm, and described as Europe's leading kitchen specialist, with brands including Magnet in the UK, Norema and Svedex in Scandinavia, HTH in Denmark and others, selling kitchens through own showrooms, retailers and builders. It has been loss-making in recent years and underwent restructuring. It is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Funding shown is about 1.5 billion Swedish kronor, from March 2026. A consumer home brand with regional recognition, notably Magnet in the UK.

NVISION Eye Centers is a US network of eye surgery and vision centres, based in Aliso Viejo, California, offering LASIK, cataract surgery, lens implants and eye care, run by a group of ophthalmologists and optometrists at clinics in the western United States. It earns from patient-paid elective procedures and insurance. Crunchbase shows about 177 million dollars of financing in 2022. A consumer health brand with local awareness and advertising activity.

Olsam Group is a London-based consumer products company, founded around 2020, that acquires and grows online consumer brands, particularly those selling on Amazon and other marketplaces, using data and technology to improve product, marketing and operations. It operates a portfolio of brands in categories such as home, pet and personal care. Funding shown is about 165 million dollars, from September 2021. The portfolio brands may have more consumer visibility than Olsam itself.

Polly is a Vermont-based digital insurance marketplace and software company that helps automotive businesses, such as dealers and lenders, offer insurance and protection products, using enterprise software to sell and manage policies. Customers are auto dealers and related businesses, and revenue comes from software fees and commissions. Funding shown is about 176 million dollars, with the latest round in August 2021, which may include debt. A B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

Resident is a Tampa, Florida group of direct-to-consumer home and sleep brands, formerly Resident Home, whose brands include Nectar, DreamCloud, Awara and Level Sleep, selling mattresses, bedding and furniture online and through partners. It is privately held. Crunchbase shows about 169 million dollars raised. Its mattress brands are well known among online shoppers in the US, with notable advertising and marketing spend, particularly for Nectar, and the Resident name itself is little known to consumers.

TARC is an Indian real estate developer, based in New Delhi, that builds and sells luxury residential apartments, commercial complexes, hotels and plots, mainly in Delhi and the national capital region. It is listed on the Indian stock exchanges. Funding shown is about 13.3 billion rupees, with the latest figure in May 2022. A regional developer with recognition in the Delhi property market and no wider consumer profile.

UnitedMasters is a Brooklyn music technology company, founded in 2018 by Steve Stoute, which gives independent artists a way to distribute their music to streaming platforms, keep their ownership, and receive brand partnerships and marketing support, with a mobile app and artist services. It has partnered with brands such as the NBA and Apple, and was backed by Apple, Alphabet and Andreessen Horowitz. Crunchbase shows about 170 million dollars raised. A creator-focused brand with strong cultural awareness among artists and marketers.

Upsun is a Paris-based cloud platform, from the company formerly known as Platform.sh, which gives developers and businesses a tool to build, deploy and manage web applications across multiple environments, with automated preview environments and cloud hosting. It earns subscription and usage fees from agencies and software firms. Crunchbase shows about 175 million dollars raised from venture investors. A B2B developer tools brand with no consumer profile.

Vagaro is a Pleasanton, California software company, founded in 2009, that provides booking, payment and business management software for hair salons, spas, barbers, nail studios and fitness businesses, together with a consumer app and marketplace where customers find and book services. Small businesses pay a subscription fee, and Vagaro processes payments. It has hundreds of thousands of service professionals using it. Crunchbase shows about 163 million dollars raised. A B2B brand well known to salon owners, and a growing consumer app.

Hoover CS is a Katy, Texas company, formerly Hoover Containment Solutions, which provides fleet management for specialised containers, tanks and packaging used for hazardous goods and energy industry materials, supplying, leasing and maintaining equipment to chemical, oil and gas and industrial customers. It is privately held. Funding shown is about 160 million dollars, from December 2022. A B2B industrial services company, with no consumer profile.

AllTrails is a San Francisco outdoor recreation platform, founded in 2010, whose app and website offer trail maps, reviews, photos and navigation for hiking, trail running, biking and camping, with a paid AllTrails Plus and Peak subscription. It has tens of millions of registered users around the world and a large library of trails. Backed by Spectrum Equity and GV, Crunchbase shows about 153 million dollars raised. A very popular consumer outdoors app, and a strong fit for outdoor and adventure sponsors.

Azzas 2154 is a Brazilian fashion and footwear group, created in 2024 by the merger of Arezzo&Co and Grupo Soma, and based in Sao Paulo, with brands such as Arezzo, Schutz, Anacapri, Farm, Animale, Hering and Reserva, sold through its own stores, e-commerce and multi-brand retailers. It is listed on B3 as AZZA3. Funding shown is about 834 million reais. Many of its brands are widely known in Brazil.

Banco Pichincha is Ecuador's largest private bank, based in Quito and founded in 1906, offering retail, SME and corporate banking, credit cards, remittances and digital banking to millions of clients, with subsidiaries and branches in Colombia, Peru, Panama and Spain. It is family-controlled. Funding shown is about 152 million dollars, from January 2025, possibly debt financing. A well-known consumer bank in Ecuador, with long-standing sponsorship of national sport and culture.

Phase One Lionheart is described in the input as an indirect subsidiary of a larger group, tagged under energy, with no location available and about 133 million dollars of funding in December 2025. Rezonate Music Rights is a London company that, according to its Crunchbase description, aims to revolutionise the relationship between music rights holders and the businesses that use music. The input gives no information on its catalogue, clients or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Rostrum Records is an independent American music label, based in Pittsburgh and Los Angeles, founded in 2007 by Benjy Grinberg, best known for signing and developing Wiz Khalifa, as well as artists such as Mac Miller, Mike Stud and Jimmy Wopo, in distribution deals with major labels. It earns from recording, publishing, touring and brand partnerships. Funding shown is about 150 million dollars, from December 2025, which may refer to a catalogue financing deal. A music brand with recognition in hip-hop and a history of artist brand partnerships.

STARZPLAY is a Dubai-based streaming service for the Middle East and North Africa and, later, other regions, offering Hollywood series, films and local content in Arabic by subscription, often bundled with telecom and device partners. It was founded in 2014 and formerly known as Starz Play Arabia. It had more than three million subscribers. Funding shown is about 150 million dollars, from February 2021. A recognisable subscription entertainment brand in MENA.

United Terra Enterprises is a company in Schaan, Liechtenstein, that Crunchbase tags under oil and gas, solar and wind, and describes as having a vision for a future, in the energy sector. The input does not describe its projects, countries, size or owners, and it may be a small holding or development vehicle. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

EVO Payments was an Atlanta-based payments company providing card processing, merchant acquiring and payment technology to merchants of all sizes in the US, Canada, Mexico and Europe, through terminals, e-commerce gateways and integrated software. It listed on Nasdaq as EVOP in 2018. Global Payments acquired it in March 2023 for about 4 billion dollars including debt. Funding shown is about 150 million dollars from 2020. A B2B payments brand without wide consumer awareness, and now part of Global Payments.

REalloys is an Ohio-based company, headquartered in Euclid, that works on a rare earth and critical minerals supply chain, producing metals and alloys for magnets used in electric vehicles, defence and electronics, aiming to reduce reliance on Chinese processing. It became a US-listed company in 2025 through a merger with Blackboxstocks. Funding shown is about 150 million dollars, from June 2026. An early-stage industrial materials company with no consumer profile.

Cirata, formerly WANdisco, is a software company with offices in Belfast and Sheffield, which sells Data Migrator and other software that moves very large datasets to the cloud and keeps them consistent, serving enterprises with big data and AI workloads. It is listed on London's AIM market as CRTA, and rebranded from WANdisco in 2023 following an accounting scandal. Funding shown is about 147 million dollars. A B2B software company with a small footprint and little public awareness.

Cydsa is a Mexican chemicals and industrial group, based in Monterrey, that makes chlorine-soda, refrigerant gases, specialty chemicals, and plastic and synthetic fibre products such as viscose and polyester fibres, and sells them to industrial and consumer products companies in Mexico and abroad. It is listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange as CYDSASA. Revenue is around 1 billion dollars a year. Funding shown is about 144 million dollars, from September 2026. A B2B industrial group with no direct consumer brand.

OFS Capital is a business development company managed by OFS Advisors, based in Chicago, Illinois, listed on Nasdaq as OFS, which lends to and invests in middle-market US companies, financing buyouts and growth through senior secured loans and equity, earning interest and fees that it distributes as dividends. The location shown, Sudbury, Ontario, appears to be a data error. Funding shown is about 140 million dollars, from February 2026. A financial vehicle with no consumer brand.

Small Vegetable Garden is a Chinese restaurant chain, called Xiao Cai Yuan in Chinese and based in Tongling, Anhui province, serving home-style Anhui and Chinese dishes in mid-priced casual dining restaurants, with hundreds of locations across China. It earns from restaurant sales and has grown by new openings. It has been associated with a Hong Kong share listing in 2025. Funding shown is about 142 million dollars, from December 2023. A regional consumer dining brand with strong visibility in eastern China.

6K Additive is a Pennsylvania-based business of 6K, headquartered in Burgettstown, that produces sustainable metal powders for additive manufacturing (3D printing), such as titanium, nickel, refractory and aluminium alloys, using recycled materials and its microwave plasma process. Customers include aerospace, defence, medical and industrial manufacturers. Funding shown is about 93 million dollars, from October 2026, and it is part of the 6K group. A B2B materials business with no consumer profile.

Alkane Resources is an Australian gold mining company, based in Perth, listed on the ASX as ALK, with operations including the Tomingley gold mine in New South Wales and Costerfield in Victoria after merging with Mandalay Resources in 2025, plus exploration and development projects. It sells gold and antimony. Funding shown is about 150 million Australian dollars, from March 2026. A resources company with no consumer brand profile, which is a B2B commodity producer.

APG|SGA is a Swiss outdoor advertising company, based in Zurich, that sells and operates billboards, digital screens and poster networks at railway stations, in cities and at airports, and offers digital out-of-home advertising and data services, with the largest poster network in Switzerland. It earns from selling advertising space to brands and agencies. It is listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange as APGN. Funding shown is about 71.6 million Swiss francs, from April 2026. Well known in advertising circles.

Apollo Micro Systems is an Indian defence and aerospace electronics company, based in Hyderabad, that designs and makes electronic systems, power supplies, motor drives and mission computers for missiles, aircraft, naval systems and space programmes, customers including DRDO, ISRO and defence public sector units. It is listed on the NSE and BSE as APOLLO and has seen a surge in revenue with Indian defence spending. Funding shown is about 7.7 billion rupees, from June 2026. A B2B defence supplier with a small public brand.

Casas Bahia, formally Grupo Casas Bahia, is one of Brazil's largest retailers of furniture, appliances and electronics, based in Sao Paulo, operating around 1,000 stores under the Casas Bahia and Ponto brands, plus its e-commerce platforms and a marketplace. It was formerly called Via, and was created by merging Via Varejo's brands and Casas Bahia, founded by Samuel Klein in 1952. It is listed on B3 as BHIA3 and has gone through financial restructuring. Funding shown is about 622 million reais. An extremely well-known Brazilian consumer retailer with a long record of TV advertising and sports sponsorship.

Creality is a Shenzhen 3D printer manufacturer, founded in 2014, and one of the world's biggest makers of consumer and desktop 3D printers, including the Ender, K1 and CR series, along with filaments, scanners and accessories sold online through its own store and Amazon and by distributors across many countries. Customers are hobbyists, schools and small businesses. It filed to list on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2025. Funding shown is about 92.6 million dollars. A well-recognised maker brand among 3D printing enthusiasts.
